title: Matching a contracted prime family with regular parameter factors
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to R$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, with $R$ a regular local ring of dimension $d$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Choose a regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], choose $0\leq r\leq d$, and put $T=\prod_{i=1}^r t_i$, with empty product $1$. Let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, let $F$ be a finite set, and let $(\mathfrak p_a)_{a\in F}$ be distinct prime ideals minimal over $I$, meaning that $I\subseteq\mathfrak p_a$ and no strictly smaller prime contains $I$. Let $(\mathfrak q_a)_{a\in F}$ be proper prime ideals of $R$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_a)=\mathfrak p_a$. For an ideal $J\subseteq R$, write $V(J)$ for the set of primes of $R$ containing $J$. Suppose $V((T))=\bigcup_{a\in F}V(\mathfrak q_a)$. Then the ideals $P_i=(t_i)$, $1\leq i\leq r$, are pairwise incomparable proper primes and are exactly the minimal primes over $(T)$. There is a unique bijection $e:F\xrightarrow{\sim}\{1,\ldots,r\}$ satisfying $\mathfrak q_a=(t_{e(a)})$ for every $a\in F$. In particular $r=0$ forces $F=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0AG0, lemma-regular-local-UFD, opening proof that parameter elements are prime; agent prime-family matching argument of returned parent steps 4--6.

proof.text: Apply clause (b) of [lem-sfb-transverse-prime-ideal-parameters] to the given regular local ring, full regular parameter system, and initial sublist of length $r$. Its hypotheses are exactly those of the item. It gives pairwise incomparable proper prime ideals $P_i=(t_i)$ and says that these are precisely the primes minimal over $(T)$, including the empty-product case. This proves the first assertion; only the matching remains.

source.place: Tag 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD), opening parameter-primality argument; agent prime-family matching argument using the stated closed-set equality.

proof.text: If $r=0$, then $T=1$ and $V((T))=\varnothing$. For any $a\in F$, the proper prime $\mathfrak q_a$ itself belongs to $V(\mathfrak q_a)$, contradicting the assumed equality with the empty set. Thus $F=\varnothing$, and the empty map is the unique required bijection. Henceforth suppose $r>0$.

source.place: Tag 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD), opening parameter-primality argument; agent prime-family matching argument using the stated closed-set equality.

proof.text: Fix $a\in F$. Since $\mathfrak q_a\in V(\mathfrak q_a)$, the closed-set equality gives $T\in\mathfrak q_a$. Primality applied successively to this finite product gives some $i$ with $t_i\in\mathfrak q_a$, hence $P_i\subseteq\mathfrak q_a$. Conversely $P_i\in V((T))$, because $t_i$ divides $T$. The same closed-set equality gives some $b\in F$ with $P_i\in V(\mathfrak q_b)$, or $\mathfrak q_b\subseteq P_i$. Contracting the chain $\mathfrak q_b\subseteq P_i\subseteq\mathfrak q_a$ gives $I\subseteq\mathfrak p_b\subseteq\mathfrak p_a$. Since $\mathfrak p_b$ is prime and $\mathfrak p_a$ is minimal over $I$, the contractions are equal. Their stipulated distinctness gives $b=a$. Thus $\mathfrak q_a\subseteq P_i\subseteq\mathfrak q_a$, proving $\mathfrak q_a=P_i$.

source.place: Tag 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD), opening parameter-primality argument; agent prime-family matching argument using the stated closed-set equality.

proof.text: Pairwise incomparability of the $P_i$ implies their distinctness, so the index $i$ obtained in step 3 is unique. Define $e(a)=i$. If $e(a)=e(b)$, then $\mathfrak q_a=P_{e(a)}=\mathfrak q_b$; contracting yields $\mathfrak p_a=\mathfrak p_b$, so $a=b$. Thus $e$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD), opening parameter-primality argument; agent prime-family matching argument using the stated closed-set equality.

proof.text: For any $i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$, the point $P_i\in V((T))$ belongs to $V(\mathfrak q_a)$ for some $a\in F$. Consequently $P_{e(a)}=\mathfrak q_a\subseteq P_i$. Incomparability forces $e(a)=i$, proving surjectivity. Any other map satisfying the required ideal equalities has the same value at each $a$, by distinctness of the $P_i$. This proves uniqueness of the bijection and completes every clause.

lean.statement: theorem parameterProductPrimeFamilyMatching {A : Type u} {R : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] (φ : A →+* R) {d r : ℕ} (t : Fin d → R) (ht : IsRegularSystemOfParameters (List.ofFn t)) (hr : r ≤ d) (I : Ideal A) (F : Type w) [Finite F] (p : F → Ideal A) (q : F → Ideal R) (hp : ∀ a : F, p a ∈ I.minimalPrimes) (hp_distinct : Function.Injective p) (hq : ∀ a : F, (q a).IsPrime) (hcontraction : ∀ a : F, Ideal.comap φ (q a) = p a) (hV : PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (Ideal.span {∏ i : Fin r, t (Fin.castLE hr i)} : Set R) = ⋃ a : F, PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (q a : Set R)) : (∀ i : Fin r, (Ideal.span {t (Fin.castLE hr i)}).IsPrime) ∧ (Pairwise fun i j : Fin r ↦ ¬ Ideal.span {t (Fin.castLE hr i)} ≤ Ideal.span {t (Fin.castLE hr j)}) ∧ (Ideal.span {∏ i : Fin r, t (Fin.castLE hr i)}).minimalPrimes = Set.range (fun i : Fin r ↦ Ideal.span {t (Fin.castLE hr i)}) ∧ (∃! e : F ≃ Fin r, ∀ a : F, q a = Ideal.span {t (Fin.castLE hr (e a))}) ∧ (r = 0 → IsEmpty F)
